title: Admission of international students – How to apply
evidence: First application call for most programs opens 15 September 2026 and closes 15 November 2026; bachelor's entry normally requires 12 years of schooling; master's applicants need a relevant bachelor’s degree and program-specific requirements; English-taught degrees use apply.unipd.it.

title: International students – 2027/28 applications (DiSSGeA)
evidence: Lists History (Bachelor’s), Classical Languages and Literatures and Ancient History, Historical Sciences, Landscape Studies, Religious Studies, Local Development and Mobility Studies, and gives calls 15 Sep–15 Nov 2026, 1 Dec 2026–1 Mar 2027, and 1 Apr–1 Jun 2027 for EU and non-EU residents in Italy only.

title: Deadlines – Admission to Laurea Magistrale with foreign qualification
evidence: For September 2027 MSc entry, the page gives general 2027/28 windows of 1 Oct–1 Dec 2026 (early bird), 12–28 Jan 2027 and 1–18 Mar 2027 for EEA and certain non-EEA residents in Italy. Architecture/Design has its own table with a 1 Oct 2026–28 Jan 2027 general call and the same additional March call. A separate Engineering subsection labelled 2026/27 nevertheless describes the September 2027 intake and gives 12 Jan–25 Feb 2027, creating a cycle/date discrepancy that must be resolved by study area. Fees are €50 early bird or €150 standard, and candidates may apply to at most two programmes.

title: Engineering BSc enrolment – 2027/28
evidence: Publishes the 2027/28 Engineering BSc enrolment calendar: first phase 3 May–10 June 2027 (restricted eligibility and excludes English-taught programmes); preference deadlines for later phases are 17 June, 22 July and 26 August 2027, followed by rankings and enrolment deadlines. The page covers enrolment timing, not the pending cycle-specific Engineering call or total tuition amount. Dates are CEST.

title: Documents required by the Admissions Office – English certification
evidence: Gives 2027/28 English certificate scores for MSc applicants: TOEFL iBT at least 78 for tests through 20 Jan 2026 and at least 4.5 from 21 Jan 2026; TOEIC at least 785 Listening/Reading and 310 Speaking/Writing; IELTS at least 6; specified Cambridge, Trinity, Pearson and LanguageCert scores. Applicants whose bachelor’s was taught in English for at least three years may be exempt if their university certifies at least 75% of courses were in English.

title: Merit Based Call for Applications – A.Y. 2027–2028
evidence: Offers 10 Platinum (€10,000 gross), 18 Gold (€8,000 gross), 16 Piacenza Gold (€5,000 gross), 10 Piacenza Bronze (€2,500 gross), and 10 Silver awards (tuition waiver at Cremona, Lecco, Mantova and Piacenza); all include a tuition waiver for the award year. Eligible applicants must be international first-year MSc applicants to English-taught programs for 2027/28 and must have paid the admission application fee during 1 Oct–1 Dec 2026. Scholarship forms are accepted 1 Oct–15 Dec 2026 at noon Italian time. Awards are competitive and subject to admission and acceptance conditions.

title: Engineering BSc admissions – 2027/28 call publication status
evidence: For first-year Engineering BSc programs in 2027/28, the page says the admission call will be published shortly. It describes the required admission test and non-Italian qualification documentation but does not yet provide the complete 2027/28 call rules, full seat inventory, or all deadlines.

title: CEnT-S – admission to Engineering BSc 2027/28
source_type: Official test requirements and deadlines page
evidence: For Engineering BSc entry in 2027/28, the page describes the English-language CEnT-S test (55 questions/110 minutes overall; Polimi uses Mathematics, reasoning on texts/data and Physics, 35 questions/70 minutes) and score-recording deadlines. For final-year or already graduated applicants taking a test from 1 Sep 2026 through 3 Jun 2027, the recording deadline is 3 Jun 2027 at 11:59 a.m. A separate 3 Jun deadline applies to the specified 2025/26 penultimate-year cohort that missed the prior recording deadline.

title: Tuition fees – current published fee schedule
source_type: Official tuition and financial aid page
evidence: The fee page currently labels its detailed fee structure as Academic Year 2026/2027, including regional tax brackets and an annual contribution range. It does not establish the 2027/28 tuition amount; 2026/27 amounts are not carried forward as current-cycle fees.

title: Contacts for international prospective students
evidence: Routes international prospective students to the official enquiry form/Online Services rather than publishing a general admissions email. It distinguishes undergraduate applicants from postgraduate applicants and provides the relevant contact pathways.

title: HySET applications open for the 2027–2029 edition
evidence: Official announcement says the fifth HySET edition covers academic years 2027–2029 and opened 1 October 2026; the application deadline is 15 November 2026. HySET is jointly coordinated by Politecnico di Torino and Politecnico di Milano with international consortium partners.

title: HySET admission requirements
evidence: Requires a relevant bachelor’s degree of at least 180 ECTS in listed engineering/science fields; minimum English evidence is TOEFL iBT 90 with at least 21 in each section, IELTS 6.5 overall with at least 6.0 each section, or Cambridge 160 (higher threshold for a TU/e destination). Selection is scored on academic achievements, background relevance, references/video, and experience. The current page states a 2027–29 call is open.

title: HySET programme structure and awarded degrees
evidence: Describes a 120-ECTS four-semester master’s, with first-year entry allocated between Politecnico di Torino and Politecnico di Milano and second-year mobility to a consortium partner. Depending on the partner route, students earn two master’s degrees; the programme focuses on the hydrogen value chain.

title: HySET frequently asked questions – language of instruction
evidence: States that the entire HySET programme is taught in English.

title: HySET continuation beyond 2026 – funding and admissions
evidence: States that funding for the 2027 cohort had not yet been secured and future scholarships depend on a successful external funding award; scholarship availability is not guaranteed. The separate self-funded page states annual fees of €4,500 for European students and €9,000 for non-European students.

title: HySET self-funded students – tuition fees
evidence: Lists self-funded tuition as €4,500 per year (€9,000 total) for European students and €9,000 per year (€18,000 total) for non-European students; living costs and travel between partner universities are excluded. Payment details/deadlines are to be provided later.

title: International admissions call 2027/28 – English MSc programs
evidence: Department call lists MSc Computer Science, Data Science and Business Informatics, and Informatics for Digital Health. For non-EU applicants residing abroad it gives an application deadline of 1 February 2027 (Anywhere on Earth), notification on 1 March 2027, and a €30 fee per application (up to two). Tuition for 2027/28 is not specified; the call says annual fees are usually announced in June. No seats or acceptance rates are published in this call.

title: Master programme in Computer Science
evidence: Official page describes the English-taught MSc Computer Science and links to international admissions. Cycle availability is confirmed separately by the 2027/28 department call.

title: Master programme in Data Science and Business Informatics
evidence: Official page describes the English-taught MSc. Cycle availability is confirmed separately by the 2027/28 department call.

title: Master programme in Informatics for Digital Health
evidence: Describes an English-taught open-admission MSc and links to foreign-student enrollment for AY 2027/28. The department call confirms cycle availability.

title: Application and Admission – 2027/28
evidence: Publishes 2027/28 application rounds for international candidates and a €40 fee for up to two program applications; English certificates are generally B2 unless exempt; program details and eligibility must be checked individually.

title: Course Catalogue – Data Science, Big Data (ICT curriculum), 2027/28
evidence: Names DATA SCIENCE as a Master or equivalent second-cycle course, taught in English in Messina. The page is for Year 2, enrollment cohort 2026/27, and lists Big Data for academic year 2027/28; it confirms ongoing second-year teaching, not a new first-year intake for 2027/28.

title: Course Catalogue – Data Science, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (Economy curriculum), 2027/28
evidence: Names DATA SCIENCE as a Master or equivalent second-cycle course, taught in English in Messina. The page is for Year 2, enrollment cohort 2026/27, and lists Big Data and Artificial Intelligence for academic year 2027/28; it confirms ongoing second-year teaching, not a new first-year intake for 2027/28.

title: English-taught Programmes
evidence: Current official English-programme inventory includes the Master's Degree in Data Science and describes its ICT, economics and forensics options. The page does not specify a 2027/28 admission intake.

title: Master's Degree Programmes
evidence: Current official master's inventory lists Data Science as an English-taught degree in Messina. The page explains that enrolment requires curricular-requirement and personal-preparation review, including an admission letter after international pre-evaluation; it does not specify the 2027/28 intake.

title: Data Science – Official degree page
evidence: Current official degree page describes the Data Science master's course and study plan, with access requirements presented on the page. It is not dated for the 2027/28 first-year intake and cannot alone confirm 2027/28 admission requirements or availability.

title: Data Science for Management – course page and replacement notice
evidence: The official course page states that starting October 2022 (AY 2022/23), Data Science for Management would be replaced by the new Data Science course and enrollment for 2022/23 would be possible only in the new course.

title: Data Science – 2026/27 degree page
evidence: Lists Data Science for Academic Year 2026/27 as a two-year Master's Degree, class LM/DATA, taught in English, at Catania. This is prior-cycle evidence only and does not confirm the 2027/28 intake.

title: Master's Degree programmes taught in English
source_type: Official English-taught degree inventory and admissions page
evidence: Lists ten English-taught Master's Degree courses including Data Science (LM-DATA), and states that the non-EU abroad call for the 2026/27 academic year is published. This page does not publish a 2027/28 call.

title: Master's admissions call archive
evidence: The archive page displays 2026/27 as its latest listed academic year (including the non-EU English-taught Master's call) and older calls; no 2027/28 Master's call is listed on the page checked on 9 November 2026. The page does not explicitly state that a 2027/28 call will not be published.

title: First-year admission procedure for non-programmed two-year Master's courses, 2026/27
evidence: The 2026/27 procedure lists Data Science (LM-DATA) among the two-year Master's courses. It is a prior-cycle admissions source and cannot establish a 2027/28 intake or deadline.

title: Public selection for admission of non-EU students abroad to English-taught Master's degrees, 2026/27
evidence: The 2026/27 selection lists Data Science (LM-DATA), for non-EU students living abroad applying to the first year of ten English-taught Master's degrees. It gives an application period of 10 February–17 March 2026, a €10 fee per course, and selection based on qualifications and, where applicable, an interview or test. These conditions apply to the prior cycle only; the table does not publish places for Data Science.

title: Bachelor's Degrees – international qualification requirements
evidence: Guidance reviewed for 2026/27 states general first-cycle entry requires a foreign secondary qualification after at least 12 years of schooling, suitable comparable-country access and any required country entrance exam; it describes B2 Italian or an accepted test for non-EU students and a 31 July 2026 Universitaly pre-enrolment deadline. These prior-cycle procedures are not carried forward to 2027/28.

title: Manifesto degli studi and student contribution rules, 2026/27
source_type: Official fee and student-regulations publication notice
evidence: The latest fee-regulation notice located is for 2026/27. It reports contributions up to €2,150 for regular students meeting credit conditions and €2,350 for irregular students, with 2026/27 installment dates; none of these amounts or dates is treated as a 2027/28 fee schedule.

title: University of Catania Scholarships 2026/27
evidence: The 2026/27 call offered five two-year scholarships of €2,000 per year for each of ten English-taught Master's degrees, including Data Science, with a 17 March 2026 deadline for non-EU applicants living abroad. This is prior-cycle information and no recurring 2027/28 award is inferred.

title: UniGeApply International Admissions
evidence: 2027/28 non-EU visa preselection is expected mid-December 2026 through end-March 2027; exact dates await publication. €30 fee covers up to two assessment applications. English-taught programs do not require Italian.

title: Maritime Science and Technology – degree programme not offered in 2027/28
evidence: UniGe notice dated 18 September 2026 explicitly says the BSc Maritime Science and Technology will not be offered for 2027/28 and first-year enrollment will not be possible in that academic year.

title: CORES Joint Master Degree – planned 2027/28 start
evidence: UniGe announced the joint Master’s degree Conservation and Restoration Sciences (CORES), coordinated by UniGe with four European partner universities, with admissions planned to open in early 2027 and a planned start in academic year 2027/28. The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master proposal was still under evaluation, so formal approval, call terms and exact dates were not yet confirmed.

title: 28DIGITAL Master School at UniTrento – technical majors and 2027/28 intake
source_type: Official department and program admissions page
evidence: Describes the UniTrento 28DIGITAL offer as two-year, 120-ECTS double-degree master’s study with technical majors in Information Engineering (Cloud and Network Infrastructures and HPC; Intelligent Chips and Systems), Computer Science (Cyber Security, Data Science, Fintech, Human-Computer Interaction & Design with extended reality), and Artificial Intelligence Systems (Artificial Intelligence with Affective Computing). For the 2027/28 intake it lists three application periods: 31 Oct–11 Feb open to EU/EEA/CH and non-EU applicants; 11 Feb–15 Apr open to EU/EEA/CH and non-EU Italian residents, with visa timing limitations; and 15 Apr–1 Jun open to EU/EEA/CH and non-EU Italian residents. The page says not all trajectories may be available in period two, central selection is handled by 28DIGITAL, and consortium scholarships are first-come-first-served. UniTrento's additional double-degree scholarships are for second-year entrants who receive no other 28DIGITAL grant; their call is indicatively published in August.

title: 28DIGITAL Master School – 2027 admission dates and criteria
evidence: Lists 2027 application periods as 30 Oct 2026–31 Jan 2027, 1 Feb–18 Apr 2027 and 19 Apr–31 May 2027, with applicant-category/visa restrictions by round. States all 28DIGITAL programmes are taught in English; applicants need a relevant bachelor’s degree of at least 180 ECTS and English proficiency, generally IELTS 6.5 with section minimums or TOEFL iBT scores depending on test scale/date. The University of Trento department’s 2027/28 intake page publishes different round boundaries; treat the university-level date comparison as conflicting and use each programme’s central portal before applying.

title: 28DIGITAL Master School – tuition fees and scholarships
source_type: Official joint-master fees and funding page
evidence: Lists €75 non-refundable application fee per application, €250 non-refundable registration deposit credited to first-semester tuition, and tuition of €6,000 per academic year for EU/EEA citizens or €18,000 for non-EU/EEA citizens. General merit-based awards include full or half tuition waivers; additional excellence scholarships with living allowance are restricted to EU/EEA and associated-country citizens in selected programs. Period 1, 2 and 3 tuition-payment expected deadlines are 31 May, 30 June and 19 July 2027, respectively.

title: Cyber Security (CSES) – 28DIGITAL Master School
evidence: Describes the two-year Cyber Security master’s track, names the University of Trento as a partner, gives relevant bachelor fields and states the 2027 first-period deadline is 31 January. The programme page says central 28DIGITAL selection applies.

title: Data Science (DSC) – 28DIGITAL Master School
evidence: Describes the Data Science master’s, two-year entry/exit double-degree structure, relevant bachelor fields, at least 60 ECTS in computer science/computer architecture and 30 ECTS in mathematics, and the 2027 first-period deadline of 31 January. UniTrento lists itself as an exit point for this track.

title: Fintech (FT) – 28DIGITAL Master School
evidence: Describes the Fintech master’s, relevant bachelor fields, two-year mobility structure and 2027 first-period deadline of 31 January. UniTrento lists itself as an entry and exit point for this track.

title: Human-Computer Interaction and Design with Extended Reality (HCID/XR)
evidence: Describes the double-degree master’s, relevant bachelor fields and experience, and the 2027 first-period deadline of 31 January. UniTrento lists itself as an exit point for this track.

title: Cloud and Networking Infrastructure and HPC (CNIHPC)
evidence: Describes the two-year double-degree master’s, relevant bachelor preparation and the 2027 first-period deadline of 31 January. UniTrento lists itself as an entry and exit point for this track.

title: Intelligent Chips and Systems (ICS) – 28DIGITAL Master School
evidence: Describes the two-year master's, relevant bachelor fields, minimum 40 ECTS in ICT and 20 ECTS in mathematics, and the 2027 first-period deadline of 31 January. UniTrento lists itself as an exit point for this track.

title: Artificial Intelligence with Affective Computing (AIAC)
evidence: Describes the two-year double-degree master's, relevant bachelor fields and expected background in programming, algorithms, mathematics and statistics, and the 2027 first-period deadline of 31 January. UniTrento lists itself as an entry and exit point for this track.

title: Preliminary evaluation of international qualifications
evidence: States that applications for international qualifications seeking 2027/28 bachelor’s or master’s admission start in December 2026; exact calls and dates are to be published later.

title: Buddhism and Asian Religions – programme and 2027/28 admission
evidence: States that the MSc activates in 2027/28; level MSc, LM-64, Venice, English, two years/120 credits and open admission. The admission page says detailed 2027/28 procedures and deadlines will be updated in March 2027; the enrolment page requires B2 English and adequate preparation.

title: Financial aid for high-achieving international students
evidence: For 2027/28 lists 8 bachelor scholarships of €10,000/year for three years and 20 master’s scholarships of €10,000/year for two years. Ranking factors include CGPA at least 85%, motivational video, reference letters and language evidence; the complete call with exact deadlines is expected in late fall. The page lists International Office contact +39 041 234 7575 and prospective.students@unive.it.

title: International programmes – English-taught degree list (2026/27)
evidence: The official page groups English-taught bachelor's and master's programmes for 2026/27, including Computer Science - Data Science, Computer Science and Information Technology, Data Analytics for Business and Society, Economics, Finance and Sustainability, International Management, Comparative International Relations, Digital Management, Economics and Business, Hospitality Innovation and e-Tourism, and Philosophy, International and Economic Studies. This is the latest displayed course list, not a 2027/28 new-entry catalogue.

title: Bachelor's and Master's degrees – course catalogue (2026/27)
evidence: The official catalogue labels its course lists a.y. 2026/27 and includes course codes and languages. It lists Computer Science and Information Technology (CM90) as an English MSc and Informatica (CTR3) as a BSc with Italian and English language entries; Digital Management appears in the bachelor's list, not as a separate master's degree. Hospitality Innovation and e-Tourism (CTR9) appears in the bachelor's list. This does not confirm first-year availability for 2027/28.

title: Annual tuition fees – international degree programmes (2026/27 entry guide)
evidence: For 2026/27 entry, the guide lists annual fees by group: Italy/EU €2,352 BSc and €2,599 MSc; non-EU OECD €2,100 and €2,300; developing-country group €700 at both levels; all other countries €1,300 at both levels. It lists exceptions including Digital Management (€8,811) and Hospitality Innovation and e-Tourism (€7,025). These are prior-cycle guide figures, may interact with fee-reduction rules, and are not 2027/28 amounts.

title: Regional right-to-study scholarship (2026/27)
evidence: The 2026/27 page describes the Veneto regional grant administered by Ca' Foscari, a combination of cash and services, income eligibility below ISEE €26,306.25 and ISPE €43,125.94, and a general application deadline of 30 September 2026 at 12:30. The related ISEE-information page gives a later 18 December 2026 ISEE-equivalent submission deadline for first-year master's students. These are prior-cycle conditions; no 2027/28 regional call is confirmed here.

title: Welcome Unit – international degree-seeker contact
evidence: Identifies welcome@unive.it as the contact for degree-seeking and prospective international students and evaluation of international qualifications; the page provides appointment-based support in Italian and English.

title: Digital Management – Bachelor's programme profile
evidence: The profile identifies Digital Management as a three-year English BSc, L-18 R, 180 ECTS, Roncade, with limited admission. The page is the current programme profile and does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

title: Economics and Business – Bachelor's programme profile
evidence: The profile identifies Economics and Business as a three-year English BSc, L-33 R, 180 ECTS, Venice, with limited admission. The page does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

title: Data Analytics for Business and Society – Master's programme profile
evidence: The profile identifies a two-year English MSc, LM-91 R, 120 ECTS, Venice, open admission and a double/joint-degree option. It does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

title: Economics, Finance and Sustainability – Master's programme profile
evidence: The profile identifies a two-year English MSc, LM-56 R, 120 ECTS, Venice, open admission and a double/joint-degree option. It does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

title: International Management – Master's programme profile
evidence: The profile identifies a two-year English MSc, LM-77 R, 120 ECTS, Venice, limited admission and a double/joint-degree option. It does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

evidence: The profile identifies a two-year MSc, LM-52 R, 120 ECTS, Venice, open admission, a double/joint-degree option and Italian/English teaching. The previous tracker’s English-only label is incomplete. It does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

evidence: The profile identifies a three-year BSc, L-31 R, 180 ECTS, Mestre, open admission, with Italian/English language entries and three curricula; only the Data Science curriculum is taught in English. It does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

title: Computer Science and Information Technology – Master's programme profile
evidence: The profile identifies a two-year English MSc, LM-18, 120 ECTS, Mestre and open admission. It does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

evidence: The profile identifies Hospitality Innovation and e-Tourism as a three-year English BSc, L-15 R, 180 ECTS, Venice/Mestre, limited admission. The prior tracker classified it as an MSc; the latest official profile lists the BSc. It does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

title: Philosophy, International and Economic Studies – Bachelor's programme profile
evidence: The profile identifies a three-year English BSc, L-5 R, 180 ECTS, Venice and limited admission. It does not confirm a 2027/28 first-year intake.

evidence: The 2026/27 procedure is limited admission with TOLC-E, spring and summer rounds, mathematics assessment, B2 English, and international-qualification procedures. These requirements and rounds are prior-cycle evidence, not 2027/28 terms.

title: Economics and Business – 2026/27 admission and enrolment
evidence: The 2026/27 procedure is limited admission with TOLC-E, spring and summer rounds, mathematics assessment, mandatory B2 English by enrolment, and international-qualification procedures. These requirements and rounds are prior-cycle evidence, not 2027/28 terms.

evidence: The 2026/27 page describes open admission, a three-year bachelor's qualification, at least 60 CFU in relevant business/economics/statistical-mathematics subjects (including minimum 12 CFU in economics/business and 12 in statistical mathematics), CV assessment and potential interview, and B2 English. These are prior-cycle requirements.

title: Computer Science and Information Technology – 2026/27 admission and enrolment
evidence: The page gives prior-cycle MSc conditions: at least 48 CFU in listed computer-science, mathematics, physics and statistics subject areas; personal preparation assessed through the CV and potentially an interview, with stated degree/85-of-110 exemption criteria; and B2 English. These are not confirmed for 2027/28.

title: Admission A.Y. 2027-28 – Mechatronics Engineering
evidence: MSc Mechatronics Engineering, two years/120 credits, taught in English; lists non-EU visa applicant windows 9–27 Nov 2026, 11–25 Jan 2027, 8–22 Feb 2027 and resident window 5 Jul–6 Sep 2027; €30 application fee, 60 non-EU-abroad seats plus 4 Marco Polo places, B2 English, curricular requirements and document list.

title: Aims and scopes – Mechatronics Engineering
evidence: States the program is taught entirely in English; the current cycle-specific admission page separately confirms 2027/28 availability.

evidence: Program page specifies open admission for the 2027/28 MSc, bachelor’s qualification, country-specific grade threshold, 24 ECTS in CS/Computer Engineering and 24 ECTS in Mathematics/Physics/Statistics, B2 English evidence and possible interview.

title: Course presentation – Software: Science and Technology
evidence: States the MSc is entirely delivered in English and has two-year duration/120 CFU.

evidence: States international pre-evaluation opens 10 January 2027; Universitaly opens from February/March 2027; exact dates and deadlines to follow.

title: Master’s Degree in Chemical Engineering
evidence: Identifies the MSc in Chemical Engineering (LM-22), Napoli campus, and Italian/English language; English curricula include Product Engineering and Sustainable Engineering.

title: Application – Erasmus Mundus CLE
evidence: Publishes AY 2027/28 application intakes from November 2026 to February 2027 and March to April 2027, with results in March and May. Exact day-level deadlines are not supplied on the reviewed page.

evidence: Identifies the MSc and its Intelligent Embedded Systems curriculum as English-taught, with a Bologna-managed local track (15 places) and a 28Digital track (10 places) managed by 28Digital. The shared curricular entry requirements include a relevant first-cycle degree or specified 42 ECTS including at least 18 ECTS in computer science/engineering; B2 English is required for Intelligent Embedded Systems. The 28Digital track is open for 2027/28.

title: Intelligent Embedded Systems – 28Digital track
evidence: For a.y. 2027/28, the English Intelligent Embedded Systems 28Digital track has three application sessions: 30 Oct 2026–31 Jan 2027 for EU/EEA/CH and non-EU applicants; 1 Feb–18 Apr 2027 primarily for EU/EEA/CH and applicants not requiring a residence permit; and 19 Apr–31 May 2027 only for EU/EEA/CH and non-EU applicants not requiring a study visa. Admissions are managed directly by 28Digital. The 28Digital track combines a first-year entry university and a different-country second-year exit university, and grants a double degree plus a 28Digital certificate.

title: International Students Admissions – Information Portal
evidence: States the next 2027/28 international admissions intake opens in November 2026; detailed deadlines are not yet published on the reviewed page.

title: Admission Calendar – 2027/28 status
evidence: Explicitly says 2027/28 dates and deadlines have not yet been finalized. The calendar is organized by degree program and applicant category; the page does not yet supply Applied Mathematics dates or confirm its new-entry intake.

title: Applied Mathematics – 2026/27 degree profile
evidence: Lists Applied Mathematics as a 2026/27 second-cycle degree in Siena, 2 years/120 credits, taught in English, with open access. It is a prior-cycle listing and not a 2027/28 new-entry notice.

title: Applied Mathematics – program overview
evidence: Program page describes the English-taught MSc, LM-40, two-year duration, 120 credits and Mathematical Methodologies and Mathematical Models curricula. It does not name the 2027/28 entry cycle.

title: Applied Mathematics – how to apply
evidence: Gives a general route for applicants with a non-Italian degree via apply.unisi.it, lists documents including CV and transcript, and describes degree-background assessment. It says applications can usually be submitted January–May and contains an admission-test note dating from 2017/18; neither is treated as a current 2027/28 deadline or requirement without a new call.

title: Siena International Excellence Scholarships – 2026/27 call
evidence: For 2026/27, offers five €6,000 gross annual scholarships for one year, renewable for a second year, to international students with non-Italian citizenship and qualifications earned outside Italy. Area D has two awards for two different courses among seven listed English-taught master’s, including Applied Mathematics; the page does not allocate one award specifically to this program. Application deadline was 26 May 2026.

title: Admissions for a.y. 2027-2028 – Let’s keep in touch!
evidence: Asks international applicants interested in AY 2027/28 to register interest and states that admissions procedures will be communicated once available.

title: Data Science for Management – Department of Economics and Management guide 2026/27
evidence: The Department guide lists Data Science for Management as a second-cycle degree, two years, LM Data Science class, based in Parma, taught entirely in English, open access with verification of requirements and non-mandatory attendance. Its listed first- and second-year plan totals 120 ECTS. These 2026/27 details do not confirm a 2027/28 new-entry intake.

title: Data Science for Management – 2025 admission regulations
evidence: The 2025-version regulations for LM-DATA require a suitable three-year degree or recognized foreign equivalent, curriculum requirements, individual preparation assessment and English at least B1. Italian graduates with L-18/L-33 or equivalent meet the stated degree-class route; other classes need at least 30 CFU in named economics/business/statistics/mathematics/computing sectors with sub-minima of 9 CFU economics, 6 business, 9 quantitative or computing and 6 statistics. The document lists English evidence routes including IELTS 5.5, TOEFL iBT 60, Cambridge First/Business Vantage, Trinity ISE II or specified TOEIC subscores, and says individual preparation is checked by interview/test. Foreign qualifications are assessed for equivalence. This is a prior-version regulation, not verified 2026/27 or 2027/28 admission guidance.

title: Call 26/27 – non-EU future students
evidence: For non-EU applicants requiring a study visa, the university says English-taught Master's calls were available and admission opened 15 January 2026. The page directs applicants to degree-specific procedures and does not give Data Science for Management's own deadline or establish 2027/28 dates.

title: Tuition and university contributions – 2026/27
evidence: The 2026/27 fee page lists Data Science for Management and places it in the humanities-social area. The annual charge consists of a €140 regional tax, €16 virtual stamp and a personalized university contribution based on merit, enrollment seniority, disciplinary area and ISEE. The course-specific contribution is not a single fixed amount; this is prior-cycle information and not a 2027/28 quote.

title: Fees, scholarships and benefits for international students
evidence: The university's international-student fees guidance for the 2026/27 cycle states a €156 first instalment (regional tax and stamp duty) and an approximate €0–€2,000 personalized annual tuition contribution depending on financial circumstances and study area. evidence: For non-restricted-access Master’s programs, the 2027/28 application windows are 12–18 Nov 2026, 12–20 Jan 2027, 12–22 Mar 2027, 6–12 Jun 2027, and 1–8 Sep 2027. title: Computer Engineering course regulations 2026/27
evidence: The 2026/27 regulations require a recognized qualifying degree, at least 36 basic and 45 specific advanced CFU (81 total across listed subject areas), English at B2, and suitable engineering preparation. Foreign qualifications are evaluated case by case. These criteria and dates are prior-cycle regulations, not confirmed 2027/28 conditions.

Applicants with foreign household income/assets had to submit supporting foreign-income documentation by separate deadlines (2 September or 30 October 2026), following legalization/translation rules. These regional benefits are competitive and are not a program-specific guaranteed award; no 2027/28 call is confirmed.

evidence: The 2026/27 call publishes cash amounts by ISEE band and student status plus meal/accommodation values. In the lowest-income band, maximum standard totals include €8,246.78 for an off-site student with paid lodging (cash plus two daily meals), €8,246.78 for an off-site student in an ADiSU bed (cash, bed and meals), €4,819.32 for a commuter (cash plus one daily meal), and €3,623.68 for an in-town student (cash plus one daily meal). Award amounts reduce by income band and depend on eligibility, ranking, service allocation and documentation. Annex 4 lists Engineering Management BSc course L0615 (L-8/L-9) and MSc course M0622 (LM-31) among STEM courses eligible for a 20% cash uplift for women; this uplift is subject to the call's other rules and is not a guaranteed award.
